newsitem.title: FRANCE: Drought cuts Algerian harvest by 70 pct - papers.
newsitem.headline: Drought cuts Algerian harvest by 70 pct - papers.

text.p: Severe drought scorched about 60 percent of Algeria's farming areas and will cut this year's cereals harvest to about 1.1 million tonnes compared to last year's 4.9 million, Algerian newspapers said on Monday.

"Cereal production this year will not be beyond 11 million quintals (1.1 million tonnes), that's to say a breathtaking drop of 74 percent compared to last year," said Liberte newspaper, quoting preliminary official estimates.
Al Khabar newspaper said official estimates put the crop at 12 million quintals (1.2 million tonnes) for the 1996/97 season.
It said 700,000 to 800,000 farmers had lost their cereal crops to drought and frost.
Last year, Algeria, one of the world's leading importers of durum wheat, saved about $300 million on cereal purchases on the world market thanks to a record 4.9 million tonnes harvest in 1995/96.
The figures quoted on Monday were the first official estimates to be given for the 1996/97 harvest, which started in late May for the southern provinces and in June elsewhere.
Algeria harvested 2.13 million tonnes of cereal in the 1994/95 season.
The severe dry weather has prompted the authorities to enforce a programme of water rationing to cut waste and save water for agriculture.
